$comment: Declaration order is priority. A death costs the most and mends the worst, a group heal covers several members for one cast, a single heal is the common case, and mana gates everything else so it is topped up last. Shopping only matters out of combat. Every cast requires `battle.active`: outside a playing battle the game drops a cast without a word, so a rule that fires there never lands, never puts its spell on cooldown, and keeps winning the priority race against every rule below it.

intents.$comment: Each of these carries its own name because the host resolves a post-condition by intent name and takes the first match. Reviving proves the count of the fallen fell; healing proves health rose. One shared name would give them all the same proof.
intents.name: revive_fallen

intents.$comment: Last, because mana buys every other line above and there is no point hoarding it while somebody is dying.
intents.name: restore_mana

intents.$comment: `tavern.levels_owned` is the only honest proof here: the three currencies mean a falling balance does not identify a purchase, and `levelable_nodes` can hold steady when taking one node unlocks the next.
intents.name: buy_cheapest_skill
